result.topic_en: The upper (sideways-written) part rewrites an integral of e^x/x^m with the Gamma-function integral and locates the saddle point s = x/m, while the lower (upright) part transforms Laplace's equation in spherical coordinates into a hypergeometric equation written as a Riemann P-function with an Euler-type integral solution.
result.transcription:
$\Pi(m-1)\int \frac{e^x\,\partial x}{x^m}$
$\frac{\Pi(m-1)}{x^m} = \int_0^\infty e^{-xs}\, s^{m-1}\,\partial s$
$\int_0^\infty\int^{x}[?] e^{x(1-s)}\, s^{m-1}\,\partial s\,\partial x$
$\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{x(1-s)}}{1-s}\, s^{m-1}\,\partial s$
$x(1-s)+\log s^{m}$
$-x+\frac{m}{s}=0 \quad s=\frac{x}{m}$
$e^{-m(t+\log(1+t))}\frac{\partial t}{1+t}$
[-$s=\frac{x}{m}(1+t)$-]

$\sin\theta\frac{\partial\, \sin\theta\frac{\partial V}{\partial\theta}}{\partial\theta}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\varphi^2}+\sin\theta^2\, V$
$\partial\cos\theta$ [?]
$\cos : \frac{\partial\log\sin\theta}{\partial\theta}$
$(\cos\theta^2)\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\log\sin\theta^2}+\sin\theta^2\frac{\partial V}{\partial\log\sin\theta}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\varphi^2}+\sin\theta^2\left(\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\log r^2}+\frac{\partial V}{\partial\log r}\right)$
$(1-x)\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\log x^2}-\frac12 x\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}+\frac{mm}{4}V+x\frac{\mu(\mu+1)}{4}V$
$P\begin{pmatrix}\frac m2 & \frac\mu2+\frac12 & 0 & \\ -\frac m2 & -\frac\mu2 & \frac12 & x\end{pmatrix}$
$\frac{x\, s(1-s)}{1-xs}e^{2\varphi i}$ \quad $\frac{yy^2 s(1-s)}{(1+yy')^2-yy's}$ [?]
$x^{\frac m2}\int s^{\frac m2+\frac\mu2-\frac12}(1-s)^{\frac m2-\frac\mu2-\frac12}(1-xs)^{-\frac m2+\frac\mu2}\partial s$

methods.what: Euler integral representation of the Gamma function, used to write x^{-m}
Interchanging the order of integration to express the integral of e^x/x^m as a single integral
Substitution about the saddle point giving a Laplace-type integral
Laplace equation in spherical coordinates rewritten with log sin θ and log r as variables
Reduction to a hypergeometric-type ODE (associated Legendre equation in x = sin^2 θ)
Riemann P-function giving the exponents of the solutions at the singular points
Euler-type integral representation of a solution of the P-function equation
